about: Coalition Builder warnings. Each rule fires when its `when` condition holds for the selected parties. Conditions: {"party": id} selected; {"cabinet": id} selected for the cabinet (never matched by outside support); {"tag": t} any selected party carries tag t; {"all": [...]}, {"any": [...]}. `support: true` means the pledge also rules out outside support (not to rely on, or prop up, such a government): `party` and `tag` then read the cabinet plus its outside support. Without it a rule reads the cabinet only (a pledge not to sit with). The schema cannot tell a Likud led by Netanyahu from one led by someone else: {"cabinet": "likud"} is read as a Netanyahu-led cabinet, and each message says so. Message placeholders: {and:tag1,tag2} joins the selected parties with those tags with " and "; {comma:tag} joins with ", ".

rules.message: Selected parties with recorded pledges to govern without Arab parties: {comma:noArabPledge}. This coalition includes {and:arab}.
rules.source: Haaretz, Sep 26, 2026 (Eisenkot); Times of Israel, Apr 27, 2026 (Bennett); JPost, Aug 25, 2026 (Liberman)

rules.message: Eisenkot said on Sept 26 that Mansour Abbas “won't be part of my next government.”
Bennett's B'Yachad pledged to govern only with Zionist parties and to rely only on them: no Arab or Haredi parties, so their outside support counts too. This coalition includes {and:haredi,arab}.
rules.source: Times of Israel, Apr 26 and May 27, 2026

rules.message: Liberman: “not for the Arab parties and not for the haredi parties.” This coalition includes {and:haredi,arab}.

The Joint List says it won't join Netanyahu; the outside backing it has offered is for a minority government that would “send Netanyahu and Smotrich home.” Likud in the cabinet is read here as Netanyahu-led.
rules.source: Times of Israel, Aug 19, 2026; Haaretz, Oct 6, 2026

rules.message: Eisenkot says Netanyahu is “unfit to lead” and has ruled out a rotation government with him; his aim, he says, is Netanyahu's retirement. His No. 2, Yoram Cohen, has said Yashar! would consider a Likud no longer led by Netanyahu. Likud in the cabinet is read here as Netanyahu-led.
rules.source: Times of Israel, Sep 17, 2026; Zman Yisrael, Oct 6, 2026

rules.message: Asked whether he could form a government with Netanyahu, Bennett said: “Clearly not. I'm going to replace him.” He has not said the same of a Likud led by someone else. Likud in the cabinet is read here as Netanyahu-led.
rules.source: Ynet (Hebrew), Jul 3, 2026; Times of Israel, Feb 17, 2026

rules.message: Golan: Likud, Religious Zionism and Otzma Yehudit are “fundamentally and decisively unacceptable to me.” Asked about a Likud under another leader, he said “No.” Read here as ruling out their outside support too.

Golan: “the Haredim will be outside [the government], that is a guarantee.” He said it after a leaked clip in which he would vote for a government that needed a Haredi party “provided that Likud, Smotrich, and Ben Gvir are not there.” This coalition includes {and:haredi}.

Liberman on Netanyahu: “Hell will freeze over before we sit with him,” and “he must go home.” He has said he would not reject a Likud no longer led by Netanyahu that accepted his party's principles. Likud in the cabinet is read here as Netanyahu-led.
rules.source: Liberman on X, as reported by JFeed, Sep 17, 2026; Jerusalem Post, May 6, 2026

rules.message: Gantz: “Netanyahu should not continue as prime minister, and I will not give him his 61st vote.” Likud in the cabinet is read here as Netanyahu-led.
Hendel wants a “Zionist unity government without Arab or Haredi parties.” Netanyahu is “not my red line,” he says. This coalition includes {and:haredi,arab}.
rules.source: Times of Israel, Nov 20, 2025; Jerusalem Post, Jul 23, 2026

rules.message: Smotrich has ruled out relying on Arab parties; he called the 2021 government with Ra'am “a thousand times worse” than the October 7 failures. This coalition includes {and:arab}.
rules.source: Jerusalem Post, Aug 18, 2026; Times of Israel, May 5, 2026

rules.message: Ben-Gvir to Netanyahu: “I will do everything so that you do not form a government with Eisenkot! Only a right-wing government!!!”

Ben-Gvir has made no formal pledge on Ra'am, but his party petitioned to bar it from the election, calling Mansour Abbas and his party “Hamas-supporting terrorists” and “wolves in sheep's clothing.” Read here as ruling it out.
UTJ says it will not support or enter any government that does not first regulate the status of Torah learners (a yeshiva-status law), whoever leads it.
Ofer Winter says People of Israel will not join a government that does not, before it is formed, pass a law ending draft evasion and requiring everyone to report for service.
